growing_specifications.description: Premier commercial vegetable crop in the Philippines by volume and planted area. High-value warm-season solanaceous crop producing long, glossy purple fruits over an extended 6–9 month harvest cycle. Highly amenable to ratooning for a second full harvest cycle.

category_why.title: Why is Eggplant classified under Solanaceous / Fruit?
category_why.summary: Eggplant belongs to the nightshade family (Solanaceae) alongside tomato and chili pepper. Botanically classified as a fleshy berry with internal edible seeds, developing from flower ovaries.
points: Nightshade Family Lineage: Shares genetics and susceptibility to soil-borne pathogens like Ralstonia solanacearum (Bacterial Wilt), requiring disciplined crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.
Fleshy Berry Morphology: True botanical berry composed of smooth glossy outer skin rich in nasunin anthocyanins and tender spongy pulp.
Semi-Woody Branching Habit: Produces vigorous lateral branches that benefit from vertical bamboo staking (tulos) and post-harvest ratooning (pag-uupod).

harvest_why.title: Why is the harvest maturity set to 75–85 days?
harvest_why.summary: Commercial harvesting at 75–85 days captures firm, glossy fruits before internal seeds harden and turn the flesh bitter.
points: Nursery & Hardening Phase (Days 1–35): Seeds germinate in 7–14 days; seedlings develop 3–4 sturdy true leaves in 104-hole trays before field transplanting.
Vegetative Staking Phase (Days 36–55): Intensive upward stem growth; bamboo stakes are erected before heavy fruit clusters form.
Anthesis & Flowering Phase (Days 56–70): Distinctive violet-purple star flowers open; rapid fruit elongation starts under warm sunshine.
Glossy Purple Harvest Window (Days 75–85+): Fruits reach harvest maturity with radiant gloss and springy firmness. Regular picking every 4–6 days stimulates continuous flowering for 6–9 months.

watering_why.title: Why does Eggplant need watering every 2–3 days?
watering_why.summary: Eggplant's broad leaves have high transpiration rates, needing steady moisture at the root zone without waterlogging.
points: High Foliar Transpiration: Large broad velvety leaves lose significant moisture in tropical heat; 1.5–2 liters per plant maintains steady turgor pressure.
Phomopsis Blight Prevention: Direct root-level watering avoids wetting foliage and flowers, preventing water-splash dissemination of Phomopsis vexans fungal spores.
Bacterial Wilt Defense: While drought-hardy, eggplants are vulnerable to waterlogging. Stagnant moisture promotes Ralstonia bacterial wilt, requiring elevated 20–30 cm raised beds.

soil_why.title: Why does Eggplant thrive in pH 5.5–6.8 and Loamy Soil?
soil_why.summary: Deep, fertile, well-draining sandy loam enriched with compost and carbonized rice hull (CRH) provides strong root penetration and balanced nutrient absorption.
points: Acid Tolerance: More tolerant of mildly acidic tropical soils (down to pH 5.5) than tomatoes, with robust taproots capable of mining deeper soil moisture.
Soil Aeration & Drainage: Adding decomposed compost and carbonized rice hull (CRH) creates loose, porous soil structure preventing root rot during heavy Philippine monsoons.

varieties.disease_resistance: High resistance to Bacterial Wilt (Ralstonia) and strong heat tolerance
